Text: Taking gabapentin with other medicines can cause dangerous side effects.
These other medicines make you drowsy or slow your breathing.
The side effects include life-threatening breathing problems.
Ask your doctor before using gabapentin with:
opioid pain medicines such as hydrocodone, oxycodone, morphine, or buprenorphine
sleeping pills such as zolpidem
anxiety medicines such as lorazepam and other benzodiazepines
muscle relaxers, sedatives, or other seizure medicines that cause drowsiness
Avoid drinking alcohol while taking gabapentin, because alcohol can add to these effects.
Some medicines change the amount of gabapentin in your body:
Antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox) can reduce gabapentin absorption.
Take gabapentin at least 2 hours after an antacid.
Morphine can increase gabapentin levels.
This may increase drowsiness.
This may also increase the risk of breathing problems.
Your doctor may adjust your dose.
Gabapentin does not usually interact with other seizure medicines.
